description: An earlier, smaller version of the reverse delay: it records into a loop and reads it back at a forward tap and a backward tap, with a mixed output of the two

params.text: Sets the length of the recording loop, 0.5 to 10 seconds; with a cable in the clock input nothing reads this knob, because the clock sets the length instead
Sets how much of the reverse tap is written back into the loop along with the input, from none at 0 to all of it at 1
Sets how far back in the loop the reverse tap reads, from a tenth of the loop at 0.1 to a whole loop at 1
Sets how far back in the loop the forward tap reads, from a tenth of the loop at 0.1 to a whole loop at 1

inputs.text: The signal recorded into the loop; a polyphonic cable is summed to one channel before it is written
Times the interval between rising edges, reading high at 1.7V, and makes the loop exactly that long

outputs.text: The reverse tap, reading backwards through the loop, and the only signal that feedback writes back in
The forward tap, reading forwards through the loop at the distance set for it, which is an ordinary delay
The two taps added together and halved

notes: the module is silent for the first half second after a patch is loaded, while the buffers are cleared
recording runs the whole time and there is nothing to arm, so sound reaches the outputs as soon as the input is patched
the reverse tap crosses the write point once per loop, and a 0.2 second crossfade covers the join

inputs.1:
high above 1.7V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the length knob sets the loop instead; a negative voltage does nothing here.
